draft.title: The economy
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum were busy trading towns. Their people made and sold goods such as wine, garum and cloth.
Garum was a fish sauce. It was made in workshops and sold across the Roman world, and Pompeii was known for it.
Shops, bakeries, fulleries and inns lined the streets. A fullery was a workshop where cloth was cleaned and finished.
Historians use these remains as evidence. Many shops and workshops in one town suggest a lively local economy based on making, selling and serving.
draft.remember: Shops, bakeries, fulleries and inns are physical evidence of a busy local economy.

a.q: What does the large number of shops, bakeries and inns in Pompeii suggest to historians?
opts: The town had a lively local economy
The town was ruled by freedmen only
The town had no temples or public worship
The town depended only on farming
a.why: Many places for making, selling and serving goods point to busy trade in the town. The option about farming is tempting, but the card shows the town also relied on workshops and shops, so farming alone does not fit.
a.clue: Think about what many businesses on the street show.

b.q: Archaeologists find a workshop in Pompeii with large tubs used for cleaning and finishing cloth. What type of business was it most likely?
opts: A fullery
A bakery
An inn
A garum workshop
b.why: A fullery was a workshop where cloth was cleaned and finished, so tubs for treating cloth fit it best. A garum workshop is tempting because it was also a local trade, but garum was a fish sauce, not cloth.

a.best: The town had a lively local economy

proposal.title: The economy
card: Pompeii and Herculaneum were busy trading towns. Their people made and sold goods such as wine, garum and cloth.
Garum was a fish sauce made in workshops. Pompeii was known for it, and it was sold beyond the town to other parts of the Roman world.
Shops, bakeries, fulleries and inns lined the streets. A fullery was a workshop where cloth was cleaned and finished.
Many shops and workshops inside one town suggest a lively local economy. Goods from a town found far away show trade beyond it.
proposal.remember: Businesses on the streets show local trade. Goods found far away show wider trade.

a.q: What does the large number of shops, bakeries and inns in Pompeii suggest to historians?
opts: The town had a busy local economy
The town relied only on farming outside its walls
The town made goods only for sale overseas
The town's trade had stopped long before AD 79
a.why: Many places for making, selling and serving goods inside the town point to busy trade among local people. Goods made only for overseas is tempting because garum was sold widely, but shops, bakeries and inns served people in the town itself.
a.clue: Who would buy bread at a bakery on the street?

b.q: A historian wants to prove Pompeii's goods reached buyers outside the town. Which find would best support this?
opts: Pompeian garum jars found in towns far away
A row of bakeries along a busy Pompeii street
A fullery in Pompeii with tubs for treating cloth
An inn just inside one of Pompeii's town gates
b.why: Goods from Pompeii found elsewhere show they travelled beyond the town, which is evidence of wider trade. The inn near a gate is tempting because travellers used it, but it shows people coming to Pompeii, not Pompeii's goods leaving.
b.clue: Look for evidence found outside Pompeii, not inside it.
